metadata.title: Jordanian National Report on the Trends in Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS) 2011
metadata.venue: Jordanian National Report (Publication Series of the Center 2013)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses TIMSS 2011 Grade 8 Jordanian sample selected via a two-stage PPS (probability proportional-to-size) design at the school level followed by random selection of one or two grade-8 sections. The authors state that sampling weights were calculated and taken into account in the results analysis. No replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is mentioned. The report focuses on descriptive comparisons and regression-based associations rather than ML model training, so the weighting is described as part of the TIMSS national reporting analysis pipeline rather than an ML-specific weighting strategy.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a national TIMSS 2011 report that reports achievement averages and achievement-level distributions and discusses relationships using regression outputs, but it does not describe any plausible-value (PV) generation/combining procedure for cognitive achievement scores. Missing-data handling is also not documented (e.g., whether cases with missing questionnaire responses were excluded or imputed). Given the report’s nature as a national descriptive/analytic report rather than a transparent ML modeling paper, the PV and missing-data procedures are not sufficiently specified for extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample is the TIMSS 2011 Grade 8 student sample in Jordan, selected from public schools, private schools, and UNRWA schools. Sampling followed a two-stage PPS design: schools were the first-stage sampling units and one or two grade-8 sections were randomly selected within each sampled school. The report states that sampling weights were calculated and used in analysis. No additional student-level inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., missing questionnaire rules) are described.

data.outcome_summary: This Jordanian national report uses TIMSS 2011 Grade 8 data (N=7,694 students) to describe achievement levels and to analyze factors associated with the decline from 2007 to 2011. It reports that Jordan’s science mean was 449 versus the international average 477 and that math mean was 406 versus the international average 467. The reported change between 2007 and 2011 is a decline of 33 points in science and 21 points in math. The report also documents disparities by gender (females higher), school location (urban higher), and supervising authority (private highest, UNRWA lowest). No machine-learning model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) are provided, and plausible-value handling is not described because the report is not framed as an ML PV-based modeling study.
